page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.4xlarge is an ARM64-based general-purpose server instance powered by a 16-core Ampere Altra processor running at a dedicated 2.8 GHz. It features 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. The instance operates on the KVM hypervisor and does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying instead on network-attached storage. Baseline network bandwidth is rated at 5 Gbps.

Benchmark data indicates average performance across most standard compute and memory operations. The stress-ng multi-core CPU test scores 28603.05, while the single-core test reaches 1790.29. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1136.7 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 122.26 GB/sec for uncached large blocks. However, the ARM64 architecture shows performance limitations in specific workloads, with weak results in single-threaded bzip3 decompression (7.62 GB/sec) and PassMark CPU encryption (2605.13). The lack of x86-specific vector extensions like AVX-512 or AMX limits its utility for specialized vector math, though it maintains average performance in Redis SET operations (21.74 million operations/sec) and static web serving (18.21 GB/sec).

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.g6r.4xlarge leverages the high resource density of the Ampere Altra ARM64 platform to deliver steady, dedicated compute resources without the premium associated with x86 architectures. This makes it a viable option for workloads that benefit from consistent multi-core scaling rather than peak single-core performance. Appropriate workloads include general-purpose web serving, database operations, Redis caching, and lightweight multi-threaded data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g6r.4xlarge is an ARM64 general-purpose server instance featuring 16 dedicated Ampere Altra vCPUs running at 2.8 GHz and 64.0 GB of RAM. Operating on the KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, relying on a 5 Gbps baseline network bandwidth. Benchmark results place the instance in the average tier for multi-core CPU performance (28603.05 in stress-ng) and memory bandwidth (122.26 GB/sec uncached). However, it exhibits weaker performance in single-threaded bzip3 decompression and CPU encryption tests, partly due to the absence of x86 vector extensions like AVX-512. Qualitatively, the ARM64 architecture offers a cost-efficient alternative for multi-core workloads that do not require specialized instruction sets. It is best suited for general-purpose applications, static web serving, Redis caching, and standard database operations.
